data.source_title: Streamlining the discharge process with a dedicated discharge nurse
data.locator: Abstract; bed turnaround definition and reported intervention result
data.source_setting: High-turnover telemetry unit at one 300-bed hospital
data.source_period: Before/after operational study; exact study dates not stated; conference paper presented 2010-06-05 to 2010-06-09
data.source_n: Underlying episode count not stated in accessible abstract
data.quantity: Change in bed turnaround after deployment of a dedicated discharge nurse
data.unit: percent reduction in bed turnaround time
data.source_evidence_basis: The abstract reports approximately 18% lower bed turnaround after a dedicated discharge nurse. It says turnaround runs from patient escort out until the same bed is ready, yet also says the measure includes discharge duration (which precedes escort-out). The endpoint description is internally inconsistent; retain the reported effect only as a flagged abstract claim, not a quantitative calibration value.
data.limitations: Single-unit conference abstract; episode count, exact study dates, absolute baseline/post values and uncertainty unavailable in inspected abstract. Endpoint timing is internally inconsistent (escort-out-to-ready interval versus inclusion of pre-exit discharge duration); quantitative use is blocked pending the full paper.
data.inferred_scenario_use: Use only as qualitative evidence that discharge coordination, housekeeping wait and cleaning may contribute to bed-readiness workflow. Do not encode the 18% claim or infer minutes.
